We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have a template (733) that disassembles sulfonamide into aryl chloride sulfonyl chloride and an aniline. The retro template: product (sulfonamide) -> Cl-SO2-aryl + NH2-aryl. So we can break the sulfonamide bond.

Our target has a sulfonamide linking two aryl groups: left aryl is p-tolyl (CH3 on phenyl) attached to N of sulfonamide; right aryl is phenyl with a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-phenyl-N (an aniline). Actually the right aryl is phenyl bearing a side chain: para-substituted? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl.

Thus retrosynthesis step 1: apply template 733 to break sulfonamide into:

- Aryl sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (the right aryl sulfonyl chloride)
- Aniline: p-toluidine: Cc1ccc(N)cc1

Check buyability: earlier we saw p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) is buyable True. The sulfonyl chloride maybe not buyable. Need to check if it's commercially available. Let's check is_buyable for that sulfonyl chloride.
